intro: Q2 2026 closes today. The pivotal question for July 1 positioning is whether June 30's close confirmed both regime gates simultaneously: SPX > 7,460 AND VIX < 17. If yes, the framework upgrades to BUY for the first time since May 14 ATH and July 1 opens with re-entry signals active. If not, the 7,300 bear escalation level and NFP July 2 (~110K consensus) remain the dominant governors. NVDA mandatory exit executed at today's open — do NOT re-enter until post-NFP unless both gates confirm. MU is the cleanest AI semi buy on any dip below $1,200 in a cleared regime. BTC flat/cash through NFP; SK Hynix hold low conviction pending confirmed June 30 KST close. SPCX step aside unchanged.

ideas.name: Micron Technology
ideas.idea: Buy MU on any dip below $1,200 on July 1. Q3 FY2026 earnings +15.7% beat posted June 26. HBM4 sold out through 2026. $50B Q4 FY26 guide represents ~40% beat to prior consensus. Samsung's $226B AI data center commitment independently validates the HBM demand curve at national-government scale. This is the cleanest AI semi re-entry in a regime-clearing scenario.
ideas.why: The earnings beat removes the 'what if HBM demand slows' bear thesis for at least one quarter. With SK Hynix stop risk active and NVDA in mandatory-exit-then-re-entry limbo, MU is the only AI semi with clean fundamental confirmation and no forced-exit overhang entering July.
ideas.trigger: Regime gates confirmed simultaneously at June 30 close (SPX > 7,460 AND VIX < 17) — activates MU re-entry. Secondary trigger: NFP July 2 in-line or below ~110K consensus. Size 25-40% of AI semi allocation below $1,200; hold for Q4 FY26 September earnings.
ideas.risk: Adverse NFP July 2 print (+200K strong) cements BofA three-hike view and removes rate-cut multiple expansion; MU gaps above $1,200-$1,300 with no pull to entry zone; regime gates fail to confirm tonight (SPX closes below 7,460 or VIX re-breaks 17)

ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.idea: Watch-only on July 1 unless both conditions activate: (1) June 30 close confirmed SPX > 7,460 AND VIX < 17 simultaneously, AND (2) NVDA opens July 5 above $200 on volume. Do NOT re-enter on July 1 even if regime gates confirm — NFP July 2 into the 3-day July 4-6 holiday gap creates a binary with zero hedge ability. Mandatory exit was executed at June 30 open; the position is flat/cash for NVDA until post-NFP.
ideas.why: Three consecutive major catalyst sessions (June 26 reconstitution, June 29 Samsung/SCOTUS, June 29 AI re-rating) were absorbed by institutional supply above $195. That is active distribution, not momentum exhaustion. Stop Day 2 triggered at $194.97. The forced-exit selling today adds another supply layer. The stock needs post-NFP regime clarity before any re-entry.
ideas.trigger: SPX confirms > 7,460 AND VIX < 17 at June 30 close → re-entry activates for NVDA at $200+ on volume starting July 5 (post-NFP). If gates fail tonight: next structural entry is August 26 Q2 FY27 earnings where $91B quarterly revenue guide is the catalyst.
ideas.risk: NVDA gaps above $200 on July 1 before NFP, creating FOMO pressure to re-enter early; NFP July 2 blowout (+200K+) re-breaks VIX above 17 and SPX below 7,400 from re-entry; institutional supply overhang above $195 persists even after regime gates clear

ideas.name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
ideas.idea: If June 30 close confirms SPX > 7,460 AND VIX < 17 simultaneously (first time since May 14 ATH), hold or add SPY at July 1 open as the regime upgrade from HOLD to BUY activates. Q2 window dressing follow-through is typical in the first 1-2 sessions of Q3 as managers who were early to window-dress in late June carry momentum into the new quarter. Target: SPX 7,500-7,550 by NFP.
ideas.why: VIX already cleared at 16.41 (June 29 close). SPX needed only +0.27% to clear 7,460 at June 30 close. If window dressing delivered, the structural setup is the strongest since May 14 — two simultaneous gate clearances remove the STEP ASIDE regime that has governed since mid-May. July 1 is a 'buy the confirmation' session.
ideas.trigger: June 30 SPX closing print confirmed above 7,460 AND VIX close below 17. Both must be simultaneous. If SPX closed exactly at 7,460 or below, do not add. If NFP consensus is confirmed in-line (~110K) or below: maintain SPY into July 5 open.
ideas.risk: NVDA forced-exit selling at June 30 open spilled into broader AI tech, held SPX below 7,460 at close; JPMorgan $165B quarter-end selling program residual overhang; NFP July 2 adverse blowout print reverses any Q3 momentum before the position can profit; FOMC hawkish stance limits multiple expansion ceiling

ideas.name: Alphabet Inc.
ideas.idea: GOOGL became a Dow Jones component on June 29 (+5% first Dow day) — the largest technical buyer base expansion for any Dow addition in recent years. Passive index funds tracking the Dow must purchase shares. Combined with AI search monetization and Waymo's accelerating deployment, GOOGL is the cleanest large-cap buy in a regime-clearing scenario. Target: $220-$230 before Q2 earnings.
ideas.why: Dow inclusion creates a structural buyer floor: every Dow-tracking ETF and fund must rebalance to add GOOGL. The +5% first-day pop reflected that demand in a thin pre-Q3 session. July 1 opens with that demand still clearing. AI search integration is converting user sessions to revenue at higher CPCs than classic search. SCOTUS upheld Fed independence June 29 — removes the regulatory overhang that had kept GOOGL at a discount to peers.
ideas.trigger: Regime gates confirmed June 30 close (SPX > 7,460 AND VIX < 17) → add GOOGL at July 1 open. Size 15-25% of big-tech allocation. Hold through Q2 2026 earnings expected late July; Q2 earnings guide will frame the AI monetization trajectory for H2.
ideas.risk: DOJ antitrust ruling unfavorable in ongoing ad-tech case; AI search cannibalization of click revenue shows up in Q2 earnings; Dow inclusion demand fully absorbed in the first session (June 29) with no follow-through; broader market regime fails to confirm (SPX stays below 7,460)

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: BTC flat/cash — Day 9 of exit gate sequence. $59,339 at 11:01 UTC June 30 is $2,660 below the $62,000 re-entry gate. Volume deceleration (986 BTC in first 11 hours vs June 29's 3,433 BTC) is the most constructive signal of the entire nine-session distribution window but +4.48% is required to reach the gate today, probability < 10%. The holiday gap (July 4-6 markets closed) removes hedging ability for any early re-entry. Watch-only until July 7 minimum.
ideas.why: Post-Q2 options expiry (June 26) removed the mechanical supply pinning that held BTC near $61,000-$63,000 for three sessions. The volume deceleration on the decline since then suggests selling pressure is exhausting, not accelerating. But the gate is $2,660 away and crossing into a 3-day holiday window with no hedge ability is a structural error regardless of BTC's trajectory.
ideas.trigger: Two consecutive UTC closes above $62,000 AND IBIT daily net inflows for 3+ consecutive days (farside.co.uk T+2 lag for confirmation). With July 4-6 holiday, no realistic re-entry window before July 7. Even if Day 1 gate activates today, the NFP July 2 binary and holiday gap prevent re-entry.
ideas.risk: BTC gaps through $62,000 on July 1 on strong risk sentiment post-Q2 close, creating FOMO entry before NFP and holiday gap; IBIT inflow data shows reversal but T+2 lag delays confirmation until position is too dangerous to add; adverse NFP re-breaks BTC below $57,000 from a forced early re-entry

ideas.name: SK Hynix
ideas.idea: Hold LOW conviction only — June 30 KST close is UNCONFIRMED. Day low ₩2,541,000 tested the ₩2,540,000 mandatory stop with ₩1,000 margin; V-recovery to ₩2,742,000 is consistent with ADR underwriter stabilization (BofA/Goldman/Citigroup/JPMorgan ahead of July 10 Nasdaq listing). KOSPI June 29 confirmed 8,395 — below the 8,500 re-entry gate (Gate 1 failed). No action on July 1 before verified close data.
ideas.why: The near-stop event on the ₩1,000 margin is a significant structural warning: institutional supply below ₩2,541,000 exists and was tested. The V-recovery saved the position but KOSPI Gate 1 failed (8,395 vs. 8,500 threshold). The only reason to stay in LOW conviction is the ADR underwriter mandate, which creates a structural buyer floor ahead of the July 10 Nasdaq listing. Without that, the stop logic would already have triggered.
ideas.trigger: Verify June 30 KST close before any July 1 action. If confirmed close above ₩2,700,000 AND KOSPI July 1 opens above 8,500 simultaneously: upgrade to HOLD MEDIUM and add 50% on July 1 KST open. If close below ₩2,540,000 was confirmed: Stop Day 1 triggered — execute mandatory full exit protocol on July 1 KST open.
ideas.risk: June 30 KST close was below ₩2,540,000 (stop triggered, full exit required); KOSPI remains below 8,500 through July 1 (Gate 1 still failed); ADR underwriter stabilization proves insufficient to sustain ₩2,700,000+ given ongoing Korea macro headwinds; US AI semi selloff (NVDA, MU) spills into Korean AI memory names

ideas.name: SPCX (Space ETF)
ideas.idea: Step aside HIGH conviction — do NOT re-enter on July 1 regardless of today's session outcome. Bond distribution Day 6. Est. June 30 close $164.19 (+7.15%) on Q2 window dressing + early Nasdaq 100 pre-positioning (July 7 effective, 7 sessions away). Still $20.81 below the $185 re-entry gate. The IG floor $150 held ($151.74 day low) — providing structural support but not a re-entry signal. Volume normalizing to est. 60-80M (down from the 200M+ distribution peak).
ideas.why: The $25B bond settled June 26 triggered institutional deleveraging that is structurally complete but the technical re-entry gate at $185 is $20.81 away. Single-session spikes driven by window dressing or Nasdaq 100 pre-positioning do not clear the gate — two consecutive closes above $185 with normalized volume are required. July 7 Nasdaq 100 inclusion is the real catalyst; any re-entry before then is front-running an event that could easily spike-and-reverse.
ideas.trigger: Two consecutive closes above $185 with volume below 30M shares/day (normalized from distribution peak). With July 7 effective date, the earliest rational re-entry window is July 8-10 (two confirmed post-inclusion closes above $185). Monitor daily but do NOT enter before gate criteria are simultaneously met.
ideas.risk: Nasdaq 100 inclusion demand fully pulls SPCX through $185+ on July 7-8 before the re-entry gate is confirmed; bond distribution resumes above $165 (another large block unwind not yet cleared); broader space sector sells off on adverse NASA/DoD budget news; re-entry gate move from $185 to $175 is not warranted — gate discipline must hold

ideas.name: Meta Platforms
ideas.idea: META is the second-cleanest big-tech buy in a regime-clearing scenario behind GOOGL. AI-driven ad efficiency improvements are showing up in CPM expansion — the AI ad-targeting thesis is translating to revenue, not just narrative. LLaMA open-source flywheel is accelerating developer ecosystem growth, which creates a structural moat against closed-model competitors. Q2 2026 earnings expected late July will be the first full-quarter read on AI monetization at scale.
ideas.why: META has the most direct AI-to-revenue conversion path of any big-tech name: every AI improvement to ad targeting is immediately monetizable across 3.3B daily active users. Unlike GOOGL (search cannibalization risk) or MSFT (enterprise sales cycle lag), META's revenue model is real-time. FOMC hawkish hold reduces the rate-cut tailwind but META's FCF generation makes it rate-resilient.
ideas.trigger: Regime gates confirmed at June 30 close (SPX > 7,460 AND VIX < 17) → add META at July 1 open. 15-20% of big-tech allocation. NFP July 2 in-line or below (~110K) confirms the add. Target: new ATH before Q2 earnings as AI ad monetization expectations ramp.
ideas.risk: EU AI Act compliance costs create a regulatory drag not yet priced; Q2 earnings miss on ad revenue (economic slowdown reducing advertiser budgets); Apple iOS privacy changes accelerate ad targeting degradation faster than AI can compensate; broader regime fails (SPX stays below 7,460, VIX re-breaks 17)
